# Josie Pye

## Overview

- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v1 c15 P22](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0022), [v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- **Role:** Student  <sub>[v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034)</sub>

## Appearance

Josie is described as fat. She wears dresses with flounces and took first prize for knitted lace. Her appearance can make her look like a perfect scarecrow to others when compared, but she dresses in style.

_Sources: [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c27 P40](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0040), [v1 c29 P24](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0024), [v1 c31 P8](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0008)_

## Personality

Josie is sharp-tongued, blunt, and frequently disagreeable or malicious. She lacks imagination and can be sulky or defiant when she does not get her way. She displays airy unconcern and confidence in physical feats like walking fences. Despite her prickly demeanor, she can feel remorse when her dares lead to serious harm.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P47](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0047), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033)_

## Goals

- Attending college for education's sake without needing to earn a living  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021)</sub>

## History

Josie attended Avonlea school, where she was known for peeking at her book during a spelling lesson to get ahead before being caught out by Anne Shirley. At a gathering at the Barry house, Josie expertly walked a board fence and then dared Anne to walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry's kitchen roof; when Anne fell and broke her ankle, Josie was seized with remorse over causing the injury. She later visited Anne during her recovery. Josie took part in the preparations for the school concert, though she was sulky about not getting the part of the Fairy Queen, and won first prize for knitted lace at the exhibition. She joined the Queen's class under Miss Stacy and scraped through the Entrance examinations with three marks to spare. Josie went on to attend Queen's Academy in town, where she earned a reputation as the sharpest-tongued student. After completing the year and passing her examinations, she decided to return to Queen's for another year rather than teach.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P25](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0025), [v1 c23 P6](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0006), [v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011), [v1 c23 P18](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0018), [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c24 P14](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0014), [v1 c29 P24](../source/v01-c29.md#nw-v01-c29-p0024), [v1 c30 P20](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0020), [v1 c32 P42](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0042), [v1 c34 P17](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0017), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P23](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0023), [v1 c37 P34](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0034)_

## Background by volume

- Member of the Pye family of Avonlea  <sub>[v1 c15 P26](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0026), [v1 c37 P33](../source/v01-c37.md#nw-v01-c37-p0033), [v1 c38 P40](../source/v01-c38.md#nw-v01-c38-p0040)</sub>
- Daughter of a wealthy father who can afford to send her to school  <sub>[v1 c35 P14](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0014)</sub>

## Quotes

> I don’t believe anybody could walk a ridgepole. You couldn’t, anyhow.  <sub>[v1 c23 P9](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0009)</sub>

> Then I dare you to do it. I dare you to climb up there and walk the ridgepole of Mr. Barry’s kitchen roof.  <sub>[v1 c23 P11](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0011)</sub>

> Are you going to be back next year, Miss Stacy?  <sub>[v1 c30 P30](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0030)</sub>

> You’ve been crying. I suppose you’re homesick—some people have so little self-control in that respect. I’ve no intention of being homesick, I can tell you. Town’s too jolly after that poky old Avonlea. I wonder how I ever existed there so long. You shouldn’t cry, Anne; it isn’t becoming, for your nose and eyes get red, and then you seem all red. I’d a perfectly scrumptious time in the Academy today. Our French professor is simply a duck. His moustache would give you kerwollowps of the heart. Have you anything eatable around, Anne? I’m literally starving. Ah, I guessed likely Marilla ‘d load you up with cake. That’s why I called round. Otherwise I’d have gone to the park to hear the band play with Frank Stockley. He boards same place as I do, and he’s a sport. He noticed you in class today, and asked me who the red-headed girl was. I told him you were an orphan that the Cuthberts had adopted, and nobody knew very much about what you’d been before that.  <sub>[v1 c34 P19](../source/v01-c34.md#nw-v01-c34-p0019)</sub>

> If I don’t pass this year I’m coming back next. My father can afford to send me. Anne, Frank Stockley says that Professor Tremaine said Gilbert Blythe was sure to get the medal and that Emily Clay would likely win the Avery scholarship.  <sub>[v1 c35 P14](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0014)</sub>
